title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: In love and near affection I salute thee with a few lines, and inform that I received thy very acceptable letter dated 2nd month last about two weeks ago, and am pleased to find that we are feelingly in thy remembrance & hope thy kindness may continue in writing when opportunity offers (although I have been deficient therein myself).

It has been very acceptable to me to hear from my native land & my endeared friends & relations there, who feel feel very near to me, & often think if I could see my way clear should be very glad to come see you all, once more face to face if so favored. But at this time have but little prospect that such a thing can be brought about. I have been latterly pretty much confined to my family’s concerns having had no help scarcely, except Crossly little Sarah. We have been favored with health for the most part, & my family consisting of my own children & James French & little Sarah Crossly accepting a little hired help from Crossly & Jacob Vickers, who are living on the place & are with their families in a middling state of health. Rebecca is feeble but I believe as well as she has been these several years & contented in being here. As to outward affairs, there is no great cause of complaint, but rather otherwise, abundant cause of humble thankfulness that we are favored with so many blessings as we have been made to partake of having plenty of the needful things for the outward support of these bodies which is not the case with a many up & down in these parts.

The same spirit as thee mentions prevails here a greedy extravagant disposition that to me, tis difficult to know how to step along so as not to be imposed upon, & not run with the multitude. There are many sorrowful cases of people being in afflicting circumstances. One of which I may mention are Benjamin Allabone moved out here from Virginia some time ago & appeared orderly. His wife brought a certificate well recommended & last winter she was sick and ailing so that she could not keep up. Her husband agreed with a woman to live with them (her husband having left her) so she goes with two children to take care of this man’s wife. & as he was given to drink, she liked so well that she stayed & they both would get drunk together & let his wife suffer both body & mind. At last he took to this woman (& left his poor afflicted wife, who is a little recovered) and they are gone of together out of this settlement, & his lawful wife is going back to her friends at Baltimore—a tender & humble spirited woman. She has been living with me a few weeks since her husband left her but is now gone— Mary Jones, the Widow of Samuel Jones. John Garwood’s mother is lately deceased (& her son in law Samuel Gatkin is a going to return back to Jersey, by whom I expected to send this letter). Her daughter, Mary Garwood, has a child, & her eldest daughter she had by Jones, is in a likely way for one in a short time. Both unmarried, that it seems wickedness greatly abounds of various kinds; that the prospect looks discouraging for the bringing up of children in this place where there is so few examples of the right sort.

It was very acceptable to hire from Joshua Evans who I often think of, if thee pleases to remember my love to him whom opportunity offers. I have often to think of the journeys of the children of Israel, how many times they erred, & by their own transgression prolonged their journey. Even so it is in my view, with myself & some others. Ah, true it is that its a world full of dangers and troubles, snares & pits etc. and O, that our eyes may be rightly opened to see the dangers & that strength may be afforded to flee to the that strong tower, where the righteous flee and are safe. I think that it is the desire of my heart that the iniquity that lodgeth in me, may be done away. That I may witness everything that is standing in the way as a partition wall to be broken down, that I may witness a drawing near in an acceptable manner, in a larger degree than what I have yet experienced. It has been comfortable to hear that there is a hopeful prospect amongst some of the youth. I wish it was more general. Thee mentioned something of thy trials which I have no doubt are at times great, but be not over much discouraged, there at for I think its said the Lord’s people were to be a tried people. Therefore with real desires for the prosperity of thee & thine both spiritually & temporally.

postscript.p: P.S. my love is to you all & to thy daughter Abigail in particular, with desires that as she has put her hand a little to the plow she may not look back.

Jonas & Elizabeth Cattle were here this week & were as well as usual, but both are perceivably failing or breaking as it called, they are under concern about Rachel Cattle’s coming home & would be pleased to have her safe back again. They expressed they took it kind to be remembered by thee. I have wrote so poorly that I do not know how thee can read it. I rode by Paul Sanders this spring.
